children: Our Bureau Mumbai: The ministry of information and broadcasting (MIB) has asked Netflix to ensure Pakistani-origin content is not made available to viewers in India amid complaints over possible release of Pakistani web series Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo in the country. The ministry has told the streaming platform to continue complying with its May 8, 2025, advisory and maintain its previously communicated position of not making Pakistani-origin films and series available in India, people aware of the development said.

The development follows opposition from the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA), which urged the government to stop the series from streaming in India. In a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the association also called for a permanent law banning Pakistani films, web series, songs, podcasts and other content on Indian platforms. Netflix has not publicly commented. Industry insiders said the platform is treating the series as a global release rather than a territory-specific launch, with the project believed to have been greenlit by its Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) team.

Issued on May 8, 2025, following the Pahalgam terror attack, the MIB advisory asked OTT platforms, streaming services and intermediaries operating in India to discontinue Pakistani-origin web series, films, songs, podcasts and other streaming content, whether subscription-based or otherwise, citing national security concerns. Legal experts said the advisory is not necessarily a blanket statutory ban, though OTT platforms may avoid risking friction with the government.

Pakistani entertainment continues to reach Indian audiences through digital platforms. Dramas such as Dar-e-Nijaat (Door to Salvation) are accessed through YouTube channels and the ARY Plus app, though their official availability in India could not be independently verified. Veto, a subscription-free streaming platform operated by Veto Streaming Media, recently streamed the Pakistan-England-Sri Lanka tri-series held in Pakistan.

Its directors include India TV promoters Rajat Sharma and Ritu Dhawan. Following the May 2025 advisory, FanCode stopped streaming the remaining matches of Pakistan Super League T20 cricket tournament, while Sony Sports Network halted its scheduled television coverage. Zee Entertainment Enterprises removed Pakistani programming from ZEE5 and its Zee Zindagi YouTube channel. Based on Farhat Ishtiaq's bestselling novel and directed by Momina Duraid, Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo Part 1 premieres globally on Netflix on December 4. Its availability in India remains unclear. Separately, two private screenings of Pakistani drama Dar-e-Nijaat, which has gained traction among Indian viewers on social media, were cancelled in Bengaluru following online backlash and police scrutiny, highlighting the continuing debate over access to Pakistani entertainment in India.

title: Centre Reminds Netflix to Block Pakistani Shows
